history.summary: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple at Jamalapuram, Yerrupalem mandal, Khammam district — the most famous Venkateswara temple associated with the Khammam region, popularly called 'Telangana Chinna Tirupati'. Legend holds that sage Jabali Maharshi performed penance at Suchi Gutta (a nearby hilltop cave) and that Lord Venkateswara self-manifested (Swayambhu/Swayam Vyakta) here in response to his devotion. The temple was renovated by the Vijayanagara emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya, who offered prayers here en route to the Kondapalli fort during his Jaitra Yatra; a statue of Krishnadevaraya was installed near the temple in 2010 during the 500th anniversary of his coronation. AGE CONFLICT: the Khammam district government portal says 'over 1000 years old', Telangana Today (via Wikipedia) quotes the head priest at 'more than 850 years', and Chai Bisket says 'over 800 years' — flagged, unverified. Sub-shrines include Padmavathi Ammavaru, Alamelu Ammavaru, Shiva, Ganesh, Ayyappa and Hanuman. CORRECTION: the CSV town 'Khammam' is wrong — the temple is at Jamalapuram village, ~80-85 km from Khammam town; corrected to Jamalapuram. District (Khammam) and state (Telangana) are correct. Alternative Khammam-city Venkateswara shrines (e.g., Abhaya Venkateswara Swamy Temple; the Sri Venkateswara Temple at Sai Baba Temple Rd, Mamillagudem) exist but the famous referent is Jamalapuram — if the CSV intends a city shrine instead, this row needs reassignment.

name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple (Jamalapuram)
town_description: Jamalapuram is a village in Yerrupalem mandal of Khammam district, Telangana, about 80-85 km from Khammam town and ~52 km from Vijayawada, set among green hills. It is best known for its ancient Swayambhu Venkateswara temple, a major Saturday pilgrimage destination nicknamed 'Telangana Chinna Tirupati'.
